A warranty is claimed from whoever SUPPLIED it. A different party from the one receiving the note needs a reason, otherwise the claim goes to the wrong door.

CAPTURED when the note is raised; not recomputed afterwards. Warranty status changes by the day; recompute it and three months later the record reverses its own conclusion.
This is money falling through the floor: a repair order on a\n machine still in warranty, while the party bearing the cost is\n left as Not attributed or Owner's own account.

Three years after the gearbox fails, the first question is always who supplied this one, under which contract, and is it still in warranty — whether that can be answered decides who pays for the repair. This screen is where it is answered.

This screen does not change who bears the cost by itself. Being in warranty does not mean it can be claimed — failure through misoperation, lightning or end of life all fall outside the warranty. This screen's job is to force a look, not to decide for you.

The note declares a warranty type, but the machine was already out of warranty when it was raised. It can still be sent — but the other side will refuse it, and the whole waiting time is dead time. Change the note type, or state the grounds for claiming out of warranty.

The two warranty deadlines disagree. The deadline on the batch is counted from the date RECEIVED, while the one above is counted from entry into service — both are correct, but only one answers who pays for this repair. The system takes the deadline on the asset and does not choose for you: a difference is a sign that one of the two was entered wrongly, and choosing for you hides that.

This note has no snapshot of the warranty status — it was raised before warranty tracking existed. The system does NOT backfill it, because computing it as of today is how a record comes to reverse its own conclusion. While the note is still a draft, press Capture the warranty status to take the current status — understanding that it is today's figure, not the figure of the date it was raised. Once the note has been sent it is not captured again: writing today's figure into a note raised earlier is inventing evidence.
